title: Georgia Savannah designated uses and original assessed-water geography
sections: Thirty original Savannah legal reach descriptions are compared with the complete 295-feature publisher assessment cohort.
37 reviewed source pairs resolve to 37 original geometry features. 3 pairs have corresponding endpoint text; lake components and partial or differing endpoints retain their separate qualifications.
4 legal records have no exact named assessment candidate in this original source cohort.
Original 2022 legal uses and published 2024 assessment conditions are distinct editions and concepts. Whole-Savannah source scope is retained separately from the original217 study domain.
The two reviewed Little Beaverdam intervals publish Fishing while the legal record declares Drinking Water; this is retained as a source-use review question. No classification is overwritten.
Richard B. Russell Lake and the distinct Habersham Russell Lake retain separate original identities. The publisher explicitly names Federal Lake as previously Liberty Lake.

rows: Confluence with Little Abercorn Creek to Savannah River
No exact named assessment feature is present in this complete Savannah selection.
Confluence with Little Beaverdam Creek to Carters Creek
Same-name creeks in other counties and downstream Fishing-only segments remain separate candidates.
Headwaters to confluence with Little Beaverdam Creek (including Lake Boline)
The source contains no Lake Boline named feature. Same-name stream reaches do not establish the specified headwaters-to-Little-Beaverdam interval.
The two published intervals form a named chain; the Fitz Branch/Fitz Creek alias is unresolved.
Comer Carlton Rd. (Athens Hwy) to Mill Branch
Review different ending landmarks; preserve full original interval.
Wildcat Bridge Rd. to Scull Shoal Creek
Road-name equivalence requires source-backed geographic review.
Georgia-North Carolina State Line to confluence with West Fork Chattooga River
Text correspondence is a source relationship; actual legal boundary position still follows the original rule.
Confluence with West Fork Chattooga River to Tugaloo Reservoir
The original reservoir/lake wording remains separate.
Tugaloo Reservoir to confluence with Tallulah River
A reservoir polygon alone does not establish the full endpoint-defined river interval.
Headwaters to confluence with Little Toccoa Creek (including Toccoa Reservoir)
Published Cedar Creek candidates are in Hart County and reference Little Cedar Creek. The legal description names Little Toccoa Creek and Toccoa Reservoir; do not substitute similar names.
Headwaters to confluence with Hickory Level Creek
The published Banks County intervals do not by themselves cover the legal headwaters start. Oglethorpe Fishing-only Grove Creek records remain distinct.
Lake Liberty, A.H. Stephens State Park Beach
Use the publisher's explicit Liberty/Federal alias and retain lake and beach identities separately.
Headwaters to confluence with Beaverdam Creek
This source-use difference is recorded for review; it is not interpreted as a legal reclassification or an assessment error.
No exact Mountain Creek name occurs in the original 295-feature selection.
Confluence with Double Branch to confluence with Middle Fork Broad River
Matching waterbody and use do not equate the different endpoint descriptions.
Savannah River/Lake Russell and Clarks Hill Lake
GA Highway 368/SC Highway 184 to Clarks Hill Dam (Mile 238)
Do not substitute the distinct Habersham Russell Lake (lake FID 65). Lake polygons do not replace the full highway-to-dam legal corridor.
Clarks Hill Dam (Mile 238) to Horse Creek including Stevens Creek Reservoir and Augusta Canal
These two river intervals chain from Clarks Hill Dam to Horse Creek. The legal inclusion of Stevens Creek Reservoir and Augusta Canal requires those original components separately.
US Hwy. 301 Bridge (Mile 129) to Seaboard Coastline RR Bridge (Mile 27.4)
Do not equate the source railroad description with legal Seaboard Coastline RR mile 27.4 without original geographic evidence.
Seaboard Coastline RR Bridge (Mile 27.4) to Fort Pulaski (Mile 0)
The legal endpoint is Fort Pulaski. Harbor polygon and river interval do not establish complete legal coverage.
Fort Pulaski (Mile 0) to open sea and all littoral waters including those on the ocean side of Tybee Island
The five named beach assessment features are local recreation supports; they do not exhaust the legal open-sea and littoral-water designation.
Headwaters to confluence with South Fork Little River (including Sherrills Reservoir)
The shared downstream endpoint does not resolve the original pond/reservoir/headwater relationship.
Headwaters to confluence with Brier Creek (including Usry Lake)
Legal inclusion of Usry Lake remains separate; no named Usry Lake polygon exists in this source cohort.
Headwaters, including Lakes Burton and Seed, to confluence with Flat Creek
These supports do not reconstruct the complete headwaters-to-Flat-Creek legal reach.
Confluence of Flat Creek, including Lake Rabun, to Rabun Dam
The legal Flat Creek-to-Rabun Dam interval and complete lake polygon remain separate representations.
Lake Rabun Dam to confluence with Chattooga River
A named component does not establish the entire Lake Rabun Dam-to-Chattooga interval.
Headwaters to confluence with Brooks Creek
No exact named Town Creek feature occurs. Do not substitute Long Creek itself.
Headwaters to confluence with Crawford Creek (including Water Works Reservoir)
No exact named tributary or Water Works Reservoir occurs. Crawford Creek itself is not the designated tributary.
Confluence of Tallulah and Chattooga Rivers to Yonah Lake Dam
No complete Tugaloo River endpoint interval is asserted from the lake polygon.
Confluence with Prather Creek (near GA SR 184) to Lake Hartwell Dam
The complete lake polygon can extend beyond the legal Prather Creek-to-dam reach.
Confluence of Overflow Creek and Clear Creek to confluence with Chattooga River (7.3 mi.)
Legal start is Overflow Creek and Clear Creek. Do not extend the Big Creek feature upstream by name matching.
